rows: A record of an external database admitted to the register as a line of a snapshot of that dataset; never a project of the partnership.
A comparator record is a line; it is not a separate kind of reference.
A reviewed, dated mapping from one publisher's own vocabulary onto a shared axis or the purpose list; the only place a shared status is asserted.
A code another register uses for one of the ledger's identities or lines, typed by scheme, such as a World Bank P-number or an IATI activity identifier.
One form of a party's name as printed, with its form type, its language and the document or line it was read from; a party has exactly one preferred form in force.
Funder-side money: a party commits an amount under an instrument to a counterparty, with states of the document that embodies it and flows on it.
A physical thing at a site, such as a plant, a unit, a transmission line or a mini-grid, with capacity, technology, location and operator.
A partnership country as the subject of a macro-fiscal observation, identified by its ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code.
A logical publication with a title, a document type, a canonical URL and one or more publishers; an edition is a document related to its predecessor.
One publisher's dated assertion at one locator in one snapshot: the first-class unit of the ledger, from which every identity is minted.
One dated statement about one subject, cited to exactly one line, with a measure, a value in the publisher's unit and one or more timings.
A named organisation in a role, such as funder, channel, promoter or operator.
One organisation, whatever its roles: funder, channel, promoter, operator or publisher. Its names are name forms under authority control, with one preferred form.
A coverage definition the ledger counts against, such as a pledge envelope, a portfolio or a plan list at a cutoff, with membership as justified relations.
An undertaking with a scope, an owner and a duration that creates or changes assets or delivers something non-physical, minted only by a reviewed match across lines.
The body that publishes a document and answers for what it states, such as a partnership secretariat, a ministry or a development bank.
A party in a publishing role: the party that publishes a document and answers for what it states. A publisher has no table of its own; it is a party linked to a document by a publication row.
One attempt to fetch one document at one time, with its date, outcome and, when bytes came back, the snapshot they form.
Exact bytes under a SHA-256 fingerprint, with their storage path; the ledger cites a snapshot, never a URL, so that what was read can be re-read.
One date role of an observation, with its date, precision and bounds, so that a value is stored once however many dates it carries.
An observation is about one typed subject.
A line refers to another document or line, or an observation cites the one line it was read from.
A project is contained in another project; containment is acyclic.
A project concerns an asset, or a condition binds a party; zero or more per subject.
A document succeeds a previous edition of the same publication.
An agreement finances a project; many-to-many, and the hierarchy never splits money.
A heading line groups the lines under it in the same document, including a method note that governs them.
A line stands in a snapshot at a locator and ordinal.
A line or an identity is a dated, justified member of a perimeter; a line may be a member before any identity is minted.
An asset is a unit within another asset, such as a unit within a plant.
A party holds a role in an agreement, one row per role, so a party may fund one agreement and channel another.
A document is published by a publisher, with an optional role such as author, co-signatory or host.
A document is published by a party, with a role such as author, co-signatory or host; a joint publication is one row per party.
The dated, reviewed match that minted or attached an identity to a line; it never deletes the line.
A retrieval is one fetch attempt of a document.
A party holds a mandate outside any agreement, such as lead agency or guarantor, on a project, asset, perimeter, document or line.
A justified claim that two rows of the same kind are one thing, such as one publication under two URLs or one item printed in two places; it does not choose a route.
An observation has one timing row per date role; the amount lives once on the observation.
An agreement is a tranche of another agreement, with at most one active parent.
A document is the same publication in another language; lines are extracted from one and cross-referenced, never doubled.
A successful retrieval returned the bytes of a snapshot; a failed retrieval yields nothing.
